request: Tell me what this calculator does and how we would rebuild it in Rust
summary: calc evaluates an integer expression given on the command line and prints the result.

engineering.claim: main builds an Engine and evaluates its first argument.
Make and CMake both build the calc executable from the same three sources.
Division by zero crashes the engine.
CALC_DEBUG switches on a trace of each parse.
engineering.reasoning: parse reads the variable and prints only when it is set.

capabilities.name: Evaluate an expression
capabilities.claim: Given an expression argument, prints its integer value.

capabilities.name: Render text
capabilities.claim: A PHP Render class renders text by passing it to its block step.

capabilities.name: Load a JSON store
capabilities.claim: Run as a script, tool.py loads the JSON file named by the STORE environment variable and reports it.

product_claims.claim: Who runs calc, and in which scripts, is not in the code.
product_claims.question: Q1

product_claims.claim: The README calls it a calculator.

questions.question: Who runs calc today, and from what?
questions.why: It decides which outputs must stay byte-identical.
questions.default: Scripts that read its stdout, so stdout and exit codes stay exact.

questions.question: Should the Rust version keep reading CALC_DEBUG from the environment?
questions.why: It decides whether N1 is dropped or kept.
questions.default: Drop it: a --debug flag replaces it.

modernisation.strategy: Port the engine first behind the same command line, then retire the C++ build.

case_sets.title: Command-line expressions
case_sets.compare: exact stdout, stderr, and exit code
case_sets.reference: the C++ build at the surveyed commit, made by `make` with the Makefile's flags and the g++ the capture records

risks.claim: The usage message goes to stderr with exit 2; scripts may rely on it.

coexistence.how: Scripts call a wrapper that runs both builds on the same expression and logs any difference in stdout or exit code.
coexistence.cut_over: A week of nightly runs with no difference.
coexistence.rollback: Point the wrapper back at the C++ build.

traps.check: Does parse's printf output, or atoi, depend on the C locale?
traps.claim: parse reads its argument with atoi and prints the trace with %s, so neither depends on the locale's decimal point.

do_not_carry.feature: Debug tracing switched on by an environment variable read deep inside parse
do_not_carry.risk: An environment variable silently changes stdout, so a script's output depends on its caller's environment.
do_not_carry.replacement: An explicit --debug flag that writes to stderr.
do_not_carry.question: Q2

compatibility.name: Exit 2 with a usage line on stderr when no expression is given
